newsitem.title: USA: Morton Int'l Q4 rises despite setbacks.
newsitem.headline: Morton Int'l Q4 rises despite setbacks.

text.p: Morton International Inc said earnings rose in the fourth quarter despite a negative exchange impact, weakness in Europe and a mild winter that reduced demand for salt on the U.S. east coast compared with last winter.

Morton, a maker and marketer of chemicals and salts, said it earned $66.9 million, or $0.47 a share, in the fourth quarter ended June 30 versus $59.7 million, or $0.41 a share, in the same period last year. Sales rose 18 percent to $614.9 million.
"Fiscal 1997 was a very busy year for Morton. We combined salt and specialty chemicals to create a 'new' Morton International," chief executive S. Jay Stewart said.

"We merged Automotive Safety Products with Autoliv AB to create Autoliv, Inc.; we acquired Salins du Midi, the leading independent salt company in France, and Pulverlac, the leading powder coatings company in Italy," Stewart said in a statement.

"On top of all of this activity, the continuing businesses turned in record sales and earnings results," he said. "They accomplished this in spite of a negative exchange impact, a weak European economic environment, and a mild winter along the east coast compared to last year's harsh winter."
Morton's sales of specialty chemicals grew 10 percent in the fourth quarter.

The increase was led by strong volume gains in most product lines. In last year's fourth quarter, Morton took a $27.1 million pre-tax special charge. Excluding that charge from comparisons, operating earnings were up by 15 percent.

Its salt business had sales of $156.4 million in the quarter, up 54 percent over the fourth quarter of 1996. Operating earnings increased 21 percent to $20.0 million in the same period. The fourth quarter increases were primarily due to the addition of $48.1 million of sales and $3.8 million of operating earnings from Salins du Midi, Morton said.

During the fourth quarter, the company sold its former headquarters building and recorded a pre-tax gain of $4.4 million. At the end of April, it also received $750 million as part of its tax-free spinoff from Automotive Safety Products.

Some of this cash was used to pay down short-term debt, mainly incurred with the acquisitions of Pulverlac and Salins du Midi. In addition, $99.9 million was used to purchase 3.2 million shares of stock during May and June under an authorization in April of a 10 million share buyback.
